The Hijrah of Hadhrat Uthmaan Bin Affaan (RA)
Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) Migrates to Abyssinia and Becomes the First Person After Hadhrat Loot (AS) to migrate with his Family for the Pleasure of Allaah

Hadhrat Qataadah (RA) says, "The first person to migrate with his family for the pleasure of Allah was Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA). I heard Hadhrat Nadhar bin Anas say that he heard Hadhrat Abu Hamza viz. Hadhrat Anas (RA) say, 'Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) left for Abyssinia with his wife Hadhrat Ruqayya (RA) who was the daughter of Rasulullaah ﷺ. News about them was slow in reaching Rasulullaah ﷺ until a woman from the Quraysh came to him and said, 'O Muhammad! I have seen your son-in-law with his wife.' 'How were they?' asked Rasulullaah ﷺ. She said, 'I saw him mount his wife on a very weak donkey as he drove it along from the rear.' Rasulullaah ﷺ commented, 'May Allaah go with them. Uthmaan is the first person to migrate (with his family) after Loot (AS).'" [^2]
Another narration adds that when Rasulullaah ﷺ received no news of them, he went out of his house to wait for some news. Eventually a woman came to him and gave him news about them. [^3]
The Hijrah of Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA)

Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ left for the Hijrah to Madinah, he told me to stay behind to return the trusts that people had left with him. It was because of this that people called him "Al Ameen" ("The Trustworthy"). I stayed on for three days (after Rasulullaah ﷺ left) and made myself seen without hiding from the people for even a single day. I then left Makkah and followed the road Rasulullaah ﷺ took until I reached the neighbourhood of the Banu Amr bin Awf tribe (in Quba) where Rasulullaah ﷺ was staying. I stayed at the house of Kulthoom bin Hidm and Rasulullaah ﷺ was also staying there." [^4]

Ibn Is'haaq, as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.3 Pg.172). The narration is also reported by Ibnus Sakan as referred to in Isaaba (Vol.3 Pg.604); by Bazzaar [from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.6 Pg.61)]; by Bayhaqi (Vol.9 Pg.13); by Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.164), by Ibn Mardaway and by Bazzaar in brief as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.262); by Tabraani and by Ibn Shihaab as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.6 Pg.62).
